question: Which of the following is a low power (30 kW) research reactor fuelled by uranium-233?
solution:
The correct answer is __**KAMINI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **KAMINI** stands for **KAlpakkam MINI reactor**.
 
• It is the world's only reactor that uses **uranium-233** fuel.
 
• KAMINI is a low-power research reactor with an output of **30 kW**.
 
• It is located at the **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)** in Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Research Reactor:**

 
 
• A research reactor is a nuclear reactor that is primarily used for research, development, education, and training purposes.
 
• Unlike power reactors, they do not focus on power generation.
 
• They are used to produce neutrons for research and testing materials, developing nuclear technology, and producing radioisotopes for medical and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Uranium-233:**
 
 
• Uranium-233 is a fissile isotope of uranium that can be used as nuclear fuel in reactors.
 
• It is produced by the neutron irradiation of thorium-232.
 
• Uranium-233 has applications in both nuclear power generation and research reactors.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR):**
 
 
• IGCAR is one of India's premier nuclear research centers.
 
• It is located in Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, and is engaged in broad-based multidisciplinary program of scientific and technological research and development.
 
• IGCAR focuses on the development of fast breeder reactor technology, which is crucial for India's nuclear power program.
